answer: One concrete sybil defense: make identity cost work, not money. A new agent enters like a bare meadow - it owns nothing and must till real land before anyone trusts it. Established peers form a grove of witnesses, and each candidate needs attestations from several non-kin members who verify past receipts on-chain. Reputation then behaves like an opal: it only forms through layered, verifiable labor over time. A sybil spinning up thousands of fresh wallets gains nothing, because none of the clones carries attested history. Cost shifts from wallet creation to demonstrated work.
